newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to examine next step in Iran row.
newsitem.headline: Australia to examine next step in Iran row.

text.p: Senior Australian ministers will examine Canberra's links with Tehran on Tuesday amid an international diplomatic crisis caused by a German court ruling linking Iran to terrorism.

Foreign Minister Alexander Downer will brief his cabinet colleagues and hold talks with Australia's ambassador to Iran, Stuart Hume, who has been recalled because of the row, a spokesman for Downer said.
Tehran on Sunday cancelled a planned visit to Iran by an Australian trade delegation over Canberra's decision last week to recall its envoy.

The Australian government would not comment on Monday on Tehran's retaliation or on the threat of a full-scale trade ban and a spokesman for Downer said no immediate announcement was expected after Tuesday's talks.
Australia's Labor opposition has demanded a halt to all trade with the Islamic state, Australia's biggest wheat market.
But two-way trade is heavily in Australia's favour -- A$650 million (US$510 million) in Australian exports and A$28 million in imports from Iran in calendar 1996.
Most of that trade is from Australian wheat sales to Iran, prompting wheat farmers on Sunday to appeal to the government not to endanger trade ties.
"Iran is a market worth up to A$500 million a year to us, and it's one which we don't want endangered by politicking and by trade sanctions," farmers' spokesman Ian Macfarlane said.
Western nations have taken a series of retaliatory measures against Iran after a German court last week ruled Tehran had ordered the 1992 murders of Kurdish activists in Berlin.

The court said Iran's political leadership ordered the killings of a group of Iranian Kurdish leaders in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant in 1992. It avoided names but said the assassination was ordered by a secret special operations committee whose members included Iran's president, religious leader, intelligence minister and head of foreign policy.
